stem.en: A foreign cargo ship enters a country's territorial sea and anchors for two hours to take on fresh water. There is no emergency or breakdown. Is this innocent passage?

text.en: No: a passing ship must keep moving.

feedback.en: Yes. Ships must move continuously without stopping, except in an emergency or a breakdown.

text.en: Yes: taking on water harms nobody.

feedback.en: Innocent does not mean harmless. The ship must keep moving unless it has an emergency or a breakdown.

text.en: Yes: a passing ship may stop at will.

feedback.en: A ship may stop only in an emergency or a breakdown, so it may not stop at will.

text.en: No: foreign ships may never enter here.

feedback.en: Foreign ships may enter. Innocent passage is the right that lets them pass through.

explanation.en: Innocent passage lets a foreign ship pass through the territorial sea if it does not threaten peace, good order or security. The ship must move continuously without stopping, except in an emergency or a breakdown. Taking on water is neither.

hints.en: What must a ship keep doing during innocent passage?
Which two reasons allow a ship to stop?
